comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C94-C99. Both evaluations support the use of Bmal1-/- astrocytes to demonstrate circadian clock dependence of Ca2+ regulation. OpenEval provides detailed mechanistic interpretation while peer reviewers affirm technical appropriateness and solid experimental support.

Perfect agreement on claims C113-C115. Both evaluations support the integrative mechanistic model linking BMAL1→HERP→ITPR2→Ca2+→CX43→gap junctions. OpenEval describes it as a reasonable synthesis of experimental findings; peer reviewers accept it as part of the considerably improved manuscript with solid data support.

Perfect agreement on claims C132-C134. Both evaluations classify these as speculative/uncertain explanations for the lack of mitochondrial Ca2+ rhythm. OpenEval explicitly notes these are 'proposed mechanisms without experimental validation'; peer reviewers caution against overinterpretation of in vitro findings.

Strong agreement on claims C103-C108 regarding circadian CX43 phosphorylation. Both evaluations support the findings including in vivo validation. OpenEval emphasizes the loss of rhythmicity in Herp-KD cells; peer reviewers note the in vivo data strengthens the conclusions and accept the considerably improved experiments.

Strong agreement on claims C119-C122 regarding E-box analysis and direct transcriptional regulation. Both evaluations support the bioinformatic evidence. OpenEval notes appropriate caution ('might drive') given lack of functional validation; peer reviewers accept this as solid supporting mechanistic detail.

Strong agreement on claims C3, C43-C52 regarding transcriptome analysis methodology. Both evaluations support the RNA-seq approach, dual algorithm strategy, and validation methods. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment; peer reviewers explicitly affirm approaches as 'appropriate' with 'solid support for data interpretation.'

Agreement on claims C4, C54 regarding GO enrichment analysis. Both evaluations support the identification of Ca2+ homeostasis as circadian-controlled. OpenEval notes lack of explicit statistical significance; peer reviewers accept the solid data analysis and highlight the Ca2+ regulation finding in editorial summary.

Agreement on claims C109-C112 regarding gap-FRAP functional validation. Both evaluations support the circadian variation in gap junction communication and its dependence on BMAL1. OpenEval emphasizes functional linkage to CX43 phosphorylation; peer reviewers accept as appropriate technical approach with solid support.

Agreement on claims C86-C93 regarding circadian Ca2+ responses. Both evaluations support the time-course experiments and differential ITPR2 regulation. OpenEval provides detailed mechanistic interpretation including post-translational regulation; peer reviewers accept the considerably improved experimental data demonstrating circadian regulation.

Agreement on claims C5, C55-C65 regarding HERP rhythmicity validation. Both evaluations support the convergent evidence from RNA-seq, qRT-PCR, and Western blots. OpenEval emphasizes multiple synchronization methods; peer reviewers explicitly affirm technical approaches as appropriate. Peer review also includes C6, C66-C68, C117-C118 on BMAL1 dependency not grouped together by OpenEval.

Agreement on claims C75-C79, C82 regarding HERP regulation of Ca2+ responses via ITPR. Both evaluations support the functional role demonstrated through multiple Ca2+ measurements. OpenEval emphasizes organelle-specific indicators and ITPR correlation; peer reviewers accept Ca2+ imaging as appropriate with solid support. Peer review also includes C7, C83-C85, C127-C128 not grouped with these claims by OpenEval.

Agreement on claims C6, C66-C68, C118 regarding BMAL1-dependent HERP regulation. Both evaluations support the genetic dependence demonstrated in Bmal1-/- cells. OpenEval notes inference of direct regulation is reasonable but would benefit from binding evidence; peer reviewers accept as part of solid experimental design showing circadian regulation of HERP expression.

Agreement on claims C39-C42 regarding RNA-seq methodology details. Both evaluations support the synchronization, sampling, and transcript identification approaches. OpenEval groups these with broader transcriptome analysis (C3, C43-C52); peer reviewers separately affirm these methodological details as appropriate and considerably improved.

Disagreement on claims C13, C126, C152, C156 regarding broader physiological implications. OpenEval classifies as uncertain/speculative but reasonable hypotheses; peer reviewers express stronger concern, with one explicitly stating 'all references to the in vivo situation are speculative and should be absolutely avoided' for this in vitro mechanistic study. Peer review also addresses C139-C140, C146-C147, C153-C157.

Agreement on claims C80-C81 regarding non-rhythmic Itpr mRNA. Both evaluations support this finding from RNA-seq data. OpenEval groups this with functional Ca2+ regulation experiments (R6); peer reviewers separately note this as important context for understanding post-transcriptional regulation mechanism.

Agreement on claims C83-C85 regarding XesC pharmacological validation. Both evaluations support this as critical evidence for ITPR-mediated mechanism. OpenEval emphasizes this as ruling out off-target effects; peer reviewers accept as part of appropriate Ca2+ imaging approaches. Peer review groups this with broader HERP-Ca2+ findings (C7, C75-C79, C82, C127-C128).

Agreement on claims C60-C61 regarding antibody validation via siRNA. Both evaluations support this methodological validation. OpenEval groups this with broader HERP rhythmicity evidence (R3); peer reviewers separately affirm siRNA approaches as appropriate and providing solid support for subsequent experiments.

Agreement on claims C127-C128 regarding HERP oscillation amplitude analysis. Both evaluations support this quantitative analysis. OpenEval groups this with differential ITPR subtype effects (C129-C131); peer reviewers include this with broader HERP-Ca2+ mechanistic findings (C7, C75-C85, C82).

Partial disagreement on claims C139-C140 regarding mechanistic extrapolation to sleep/wake states. OpenEval classifies as supported but notes extrapolation from in vitro to in vivo; peer reviewers express concern about speculative in vivo references, with one reviewer stating such references 'should be absolutely avoided' without in vivo experimental validation.

Agreement on claims C130-C131 regarding ITPR2 as primary driver of circadian Ca2+ responses. Both evaluations support this conclusion. OpenEval notes direct ITPR2 knockdown would strengthen evidence; peer reviewers accept as part of solid experimental findings on circadian Ca2+ regulation.

Disagreement on claims C146-C147 regarding functional implications for astrocyte networks. OpenEval classifies as uncertain/speculative interpretation requiring validation; peer reviewers express stronger concern about overinterpretation, with explicit caution against speculative in vivo references in this in vitro mechanistic study.

Agreement on claim C142 regarding circadian CX43 phosphorylation and gap junction communication. Both evaluations support this experimental finding. OpenEval groups this with broader interpretive model (C141-C147); peer reviewers accept the functional gap junction data as appropriate with solid support.

Agreement on claim C135 regarding experimental observation of circadian Ca2+ responses. Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval groups this with broader literature contextualization (C136-C140); peer reviewers accept as part of demonstrated circadian regulation of calcium responses.

Agreement on claim C117 regarding phase relationship between Herp and Per2. Both evaluations support this as evidence for direct circadian regulation. OpenEval groups this with E-box analysis (C119-C122); peer reviewers include this with broader HERP rhythmicity and BMAL1 dependency findings (C5-C6, C55-C68, C118).

Peer reviewers separately evaluate claim C101 regarding CX43 as the primary connexin in astrocytes, accepting this as appropriate technical finding with solid support. OpenEval does not separately evaluate this claim, likely considering it as background/context for the CX43 phosphorylation experiments.
